attempts.rationale: Start with a robust weighted combination using inverse error, since the series is trend-dominated and ranking unstable; inverse_error can adapt to model strengths.
test a different weighting method (softmax_neg_error) to see if a more smoothed weighting improves robustness for this trend‑dominated series.
Test a simple mean combination to check if a robust unweighted average beats the weighted models, given the trend‑dominated regime and unstable ranking.
The series is trend dominated and ranking unstable; a robust trimmed mean may outperform simple mean by downweighting outlier models.
test a different kind of combination – the deterministic Bayesian average (dba) which may better handle unstable ranking in this trend‑dominated series.
ranking is unstable and several correlated groups exist; a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture complementary strengths across horizons.
The series is trend dominated with unstable ranking; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting might capture changing strengths across horizons.
The ranking is unstable and the series is trend-dominated, so a forward‑selection based weighting that adapts to complementary errors may improve robustness.
test a robust weighted combo on a smaller, more stable pool (pool4) using softmax weights to see if reducing model set improves performance.
The series is trend-dominated and ranking is unstable; a robust optimizer like DBA on a reduced, stable pool might improve robustness.

Test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k mean per horizon (w8) on the full pool to see if horizon‑specific weighting improves over trimmed mean, given unstable ranking and strong trend dominance.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9892. Series context: trend strength 0.864 and seasonal strength 0.1136; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.123); 5 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.899.
